speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. You've mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to help narrow down the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

Have you noticed any other changes, such as numbness spreading to your face or leg, or any trouble speaking?

Did these symptoms come on suddenly, or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) causing right arm weakness and decreased sensation.

I suspect a malignancy given your history of smoking, weight loss, and the progressive nature of your symptoms. Can you describe exactly where the pain or numbness is located, and does it radiate down into your hand? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
